title: Schemeness over an algebraic closure from schemeness over an extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], with algebraic closure $\overline{k}$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] whose relative diagonal $X\to X\times_kX$ is quasi-compact: every scheme base change is a quasi-compact morphism, meaning that the inverse image of any quasi-compact open subset is quasi-compact. If there exists a field extension $K/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] for which $X_K=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ is represented by a scheme, then $X_{\overline{k}}$ is represented by a scheme. Fibre products of spaces are [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. No quasi-compactness or finite-type hypothesis is imposed on $X$.

proof.text: The affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is absolutely quasi-separated, so the relative diagonal hypothesis and the quasi-separated-source permanence lemma make $X$ absolutely quasi-separated. Choose a set-indexed Zariski cover $X=\bigcup_i V_i$ where each $V_i$ has a surjective etale chart from an affine scheme. Thus each $V_i$ is quasi-compact; the open-subspace permanence lemma makes it quasi-separated. The open immersion $V_i\hookrightarrow X$ stays an open immersion on every scheme test. In particular $(V_i)_K$ is an open subscheme of the scheme $X_K$. Fix one $V=V_i$; steps 2--5 prove that $V_{\overline{k}}$ is a scheme.

proof.text: Let $I$ be the set of finitely generated $k$-subalgebras $A\subseteq K$, ordered by inclusion. It is nonempty since it contains $k$, and is directed since the algebra generated by the union of two finite generating lists contains both subalgebras. Every element of $K$ lies in $k[a]$, so $\varinjlim_{A\in I}A=K$. Put $V_A=V\times_k\operatorname{Spec}A$. The affine schemes $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are qcqs; the qcqs fibre-product lemma therefore makes every $V_A$ qcqs. For $A\subseteq B$, the map $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine since both schemes are affine. Its base change $V_B\to V_A$ is affine by affine permanence for spaces.

source.place: Tag 0B84 (lemma-when-scheme-after-base-change), write K as the colimit of finitely generated k-subalgebras

proof.text: The sheaf limit of the system $V_A$ is $V_K$. Indeed, on any $k$-scheme $T$, a compatible family of maps $T\to V_A$ consists of one map $v:T\to V$ and compatible $k$-algebra maps $A\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. The affine-target bijection gives this description of the second projections. Because $K=\bigcup A$, those ring maps give exactly one $k$-algebra map $K\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$, hence one map $T\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. The pair with $v$ is exactly a section of $V_K(T)$. These bijections commute with restriction in $T$, so they identify the sheaf limit with $V_K$.

Apply eventual schematicity to the small nonempty directed system $(V_A)$: its stages are qcqs, its transition maps are affine, and its sheaf limit $V_K$ is a scheme by step 1. Consequently $V_A$ is a scheme for some finitely generated $k$-subalgebra $A\subseteq K$.

The ring $A$ is nontrivial since it is a unital subring of the field $K$. Choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset A$. The quotient $L=A/\mathfrak m$ is a field and is generated as a $k$-algebra by the images of the finite generating list for $A$. Zariski's lemma makes $L/k$ finite-dimensional. For each $a\in L$, linear dependence among $1,a,\ldots,a^d$, where $d=\dim_kL$, gives a nonzero polynomial over $k$ vanishing at $a$; hence $L/k$ is algebraic. The algebraic-extension embedding lemma, applied to the fixed map $k\to\overline{k}$, gives a $k$-homomorphism $L\to\overline{k}$. Compose with $A\to L$ to obtain $A\to\overline{k}$. Both $V_A$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\overline{k}$ are schemes, so their scheme fibre product over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ exists. On every scheme test its sections are exactly pairs defining $V\times_k\operatorname{Spec}\overline{k}$; thus this scheme represents $V_{\overline{k}}$.

proof.text: Apply steps 2--5 to every member of the cover in step 1. The base-changed family $\{(V_i)_{\overline{k}}\to X_{\overline{k}}\}$ still covers, by stability of etale coverings under base change, and each inclusion is a representable open immersion by the definition of open subspace. Its members are schemes. The algebraic-space sheaf is a Zariski sheaf, since every Zariski covering is an fppf covering. The representability criterion for a Zariski sheaf covered by representable open subfunctors now shows that $X_{\overline{k}}$ is a scheme. An empty cover causes no exception: it represents the empty scheme. No finite subcover of $X$ and no common algebra $A$ for different $V_i$ is needed.
